sources.entry: GitHub Desktop - Simple collaboration from your desktop.

summary.one_liner: GitHub Desktop is an open-source, Electron-based desktop app for working with GitHub, written in TypeScript and React.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes GitHub Desktop as an open-source GitHub client built on Electron, written in TypeScript and using React. It provides official installers for macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Windows (including a machine-wide install and ARM64 beta). A beta channel offers early builds for testing new features. Past releases can be found, though auto-update will pull the latest version after installing an older one. Community package managers are listed for installing on Windows (winget, Chocolatey) and macOS (Homebrew cask). The README also points to CONTRIBUTING.md, a setup.md guide for building from source, and a help-wanted label for contributors.
use_cases: manage git repositories with a graphical interface
collaborate on GitHub projects from the desktop
install GitHub Desktop on macOS or Windows
test beta builds of a GitHub client
contribute to an open-source Electron app
how_to_run: Download the official macOS or Windows installer from the project's download links
To build from source, follow setup.md and CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository
notable: Official installers for macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Windows, plus a beta channel
Community installs via winget, Chocolatey, and Homebrew
Built with Electron, TypeScript, and React
MIT-licensed, with GitHub trademarks and logos excluded from the grant
caveats: Linux is not officially supported; Linux installers come from a community fork (shiftkey/desktop)
Auto-update will move past releases to the latest version after installation
Maintainers are limited in time and resources, so support for individual issues is not guaranteed
keywords: push and pull commits without terminal
